subproblem.title: Compactness of sets with locally uniformly bounded perimeter (Simon Ch. 2, 2.6, for indicator functions)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and let F_i ⊆ ℝ^m (i ∈ ℕ) be measurable sets. Assume that for every R > 0 there are c ∈ ℝ and i_R such that for every i ≥ i_R and every C^∞ vector field φ : ℝ^m → ℝ^m (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ ball(0, R) and |φ(v)| ≤ 1 for all v, one has ∫_{F_i} div φ dL^m ≤ c, where div φ(v) = trace Dφ(v) and L^m is Lebesgue measure. Then there are a strictly increasing σ : ℕ → ℕ and a measurable F' ⊆ ℝ^m such that L^m((F_{σ(i)} Δ F') ∩ ball(0, R)) → 0 as i → ∞ for every R ∈ ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (F : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)), (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i)) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᶠ i in atTop, ∀ φ : Euclid m → Euclid m, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ ball 0 R → (∀ v, ‖φ v‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ v in F i, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid m) (fderiv ℝ φ v).toLinearMap ≤ c) → ∃ (σ : ℕ → ℕ) (F' : Set (Euclid m)), StrictMono σ ∧ MeasurableSet F' ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, Tendsto (fun i => volume (symmDiff (F (σ i)) F' ∩ ball 0 R)) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 2.6 (Compactness Theorem for BV functions, chapter-02.txt lines 598–625), applied to the indicator functions u_i = 1_{F_i}, with the mollifier facts of Simon Ch. 2, 2.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 521–545). Simon refers to [GT01, Theorem 7.22] for the precompactness ("mollification and Arzelà's theorem"); since the Arzelà–Ascoli theorem is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, the precompactness is proved with cube averages (the elementary Kolmogorov–Riesz argument), using the same mollification estimate. This is the compactness used in step 9 of the supplied proof of the parent node. No sibling child is used.

Notation. L^m = volume on ℝ^m = Euclid m; B_R := ball(0, R); u_i := 1_{F_i}; ‖f‖_{1,S} := ∫_S |f| dL^m; div φ := trace(Dφ). A field φ is admissible for radius R if it is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ B_R and |φ| ≤ 1. For R > 0 let c(R) and i_R be as in the hypothesis. Since −φ is admissible whenever φ is, |∫_{F_i} div φ| ≤ c(R) for i ≥ i_R; taking φ = 0 shows c(R) ≥ 0. A field admissible for R is admissible for every R' ≥ R.

0. (m = 0.) ℝ^0 is a single point, so each F_i is ∅ or ℝ^0; one of the two values occurs for infinitely many i, which gives σ with F_{σ(i)} constant =: F' and (F_{σ(i)} Δ F') ∩ B_R = ∅. From now on m ≥ 1.

1. (Mollifier.) Fix ρ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^m) with ρ ≥ 0, ρ(−z) = ρ(z), tsupport ρ ⊆ closedBall(0, 1) and ∫ρ = 1. Construction: let b be the ContDiffBump centred at 0 with inner radius 1/2 and outer radius 1. It is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, even (ContDiffBump.neg: b(−z) = b(z)), support b = ball(0, 1) (ContDiffBump.support_eq) and tsupport b = closedBall(0, 1) (ContDiffBump.tsupport_eq); this closed ball is not contained in the open ball ball(0, 1), so only the closed-ball bound is claimed. b is continuous with compact support, hence integrable, and ∫b > 0 by integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, because its support ball(0, 1) has positive Lebesgue measure (Metric.measure_ball_pos). Put ρ := (∫b)^{−1}·b. Multiplication by the positive constant (∫b)^{−1} preserves smoothness, nonnegativity, evenness and the support, so tsupport ρ = closedBall(0, 1), and ∫ρ = 1. For 0 < ε ≤ 1/2 put ρ_ε(z) := ε^{−m}ρ(z/ε): smooth, even, ≥ 0, tsupport ρ_ε = ε·tsupport ρ = closedBall(0, ε), and ∫ρ_ε = ε^{−m}·ε^m·∫ρ = 1 (change of variables z = εz', Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul_of_nonneg). Below only the bound tsupport ρ_ε ⊆ closedBall(0, ε), i.e. ρ_ε(z) = 0 for |z| > ε, is used (in steps 2 and 3). For a bounded measurable f put f_ε := ρ_ε ⋆ f, f_ε(v) = ∫ρ_ε(z)f(v − z) dz. f_ε is C^∞, its derivatives are obtained by differentiating ρ_ε (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), and |f| ≤ 1 implies |f_ε| ≤ 1.

2. (L¹ convergence of mollifications.) If F ⊆ ℝ^m is measurable, f := 1_F and R > 0, then ‖f_ε − f‖_{1,B_R} → 0 as ε → 0 (only f = u_i is needed). Indeed f_ε(v) − f(v) = ∫ρ_ε(z)(f(v − z) − f(v)) dz, so by Tonelli ‖f_ε − f‖_{1,B_R} ≤ sup_{|z|≤ε}∫_{B_R}|f(v − z) − f(v)| dv, and translations are continuous in L¹: given η > 0, put A := F ∩ B_{R+1}, a measurable set of finite measure. By regularity of Lebesgue measure choose a compact K ⊆ A with L^m(A ∖ K) < η/2 (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt) and an open O ⊇ A with L^m(O ∖ A) < η/2 (MeasurableSet.exists_isOpen_sdiff_lt); as O ∖ K ⊆ (O ∖ A) ∪ (A ∖ K), L^m(O ∖ K) < η. Choose a continuous g : ℝ^m → [0, 1] with compact support, g = 1 on K and g = 0 on ℝ^m ∖ O (exists_continuous_one_zero_of_isCompact applied to the compact set K and the closed set ℝ^m ∖ O, which are disjoint). Then 1_A and g agree on K (both 1) and off O (both 0) and differ by at most 1 on O ∖ K, so ∫|1_A − g| dL^m ≤ L^m(O ∖ K) < η. For |z| ≤ 1 and v ∈ B_R we have v, v − z ∈ B_{R+1}, so f(v − z) = 1_A(v − z) and f(v) = 1_A(v); by the triangle inequality and translation invariance of L^m, ∫_{B_R}|f(v − z) − f(v)| dv ≤ 2∫|1_A − g| dL^m + ∫_{B_R}|g(v − z) − g(v)| dv ≤ 2η + ∫_{B_R}|g(v − z) − g(v)| dv, and the last integral tends to 0 as z → 0 because g is uniformly continuous with compact support. Hence limsup_{ε→0}‖f_ε − f‖_{1,B_R} ≤ 2η for every η > 0.

3. (Gradient bound.) Let R > 0, i ≥ i_{R+2} and 0 < ε ≤ 1/2, and let Gr be the gradient of (u_i)_ε: the C^∞ vector field with Gr(v)·h = D(u_i)_ε(v)h for all h, i.e. Gr(v) := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Euclid m)).symm(D(u_i)_ε(v)). Then ∫_{B_{R+1}}|Gr| ≤ c(R + 2). Proof: let ψ be a C^∞ vector field with tsupport ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, R + 1) and |ψ| ≤ 1. Integration by parts (ψ has compact support and (u_i)_ε is smooth) gives ∫Gr·ψ = −∫(u_i)_ε div ψ: for each coordinate j, ∫∂_j(u_i)_ε·ψ_j = −∫(u_i)_ε·∂_jψ_j by Fubini (integral_prod) and the one-dimensional formula integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_integrable along the lines parallel to e_j, after transporting Euclid m to ℝ × ℝ^{m−1} (the j-th coordinate split off) by the measure-preserving maps PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp and MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove. By Fubini and evenness of ρ_ε, ∫(ρ_ε ⋆ u_i) div ψ = ∫u_i·(ρ_ε ⋆ div ψ), and ρ_ε ⋆ div ψ = div(ρ_ε ⋆ ψ): by HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right, D(ρ_ε ⋆ ψ)(v) = ∫ρ_ε(z)Dψ(v − z) dz (a convolution with values in linear maps), and the trace, a continuous linear map on this finite-dimensional space, commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm). The field ψ_ε := ρ_ε ⋆ ψ is C^∞ with compact support, |ψ_ε| ≤ ∫ρ_ε·|ψ| ≤ 1 and tsupport ψ_ε ⊆ tsupport ρ_ε + tsupport ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, ε) + closedBall(0, R + 1) = closedBall(0, R + 1 + ε) ⊆ B_{R+2} (support(ρ_ε ⋆ ψ) ⊆ support ρ_ε + support ψ by support_convolution_subset, and the sum of the two compact sets tsupport ρ_ε and tsupport ψ is compact, hence closed; ε ≤ 1/2); so −ψ_ε is admissible for radius R + 2 and ∫Gr·ψ = ∫_{F_i} div(−ψ_ε) ≤ c(R + 2). Now take ψ := χ_N·Gr/√(|Gr|² + θ²) with θ > 0, N ∈ ℕ, N ≥ 1, and χ_N(v) := smoothTransition(N((R + 1)² − |v|²)/(R + 1)²) (C^∞, 0 ≤ χ_N ≤ 1, χ_N = 0 outside B_{R+1}, so tsupport χ_N ⊆ closedBall(0, R + 1), and χ_N increases to 1 on B_{R+1} as N → ∞). It is of the above kind (C^∞, tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport χ_N ⊆ closedBall(0, R + 1), |ψ| ≤ 1), so ∫χ_N|Gr|²/√(|Gr|² + θ²) ≤ c(R + 2). Letting θ ↓ 0 and then N → ∞ (monotone convergence: |Gr|²/√(|Gr|² + θ²) increases to |Gr| as θ decreases to 0, and χ_N increases to 1_{B_{R+1}}) gives ∫_{B_{R+1}}|Gr| ≤ c(R + 2).

4. (Translation estimate.) For R > 0, i ≥ i_{R+2} and h ∈ ℝ^m with |h| ≤ 1: ∫_{B_R}|u_i(v + h) − u_i(v)| dv ≤ c(R + 2)|h|. Proof: for 0 < ε ≤ 1/2, (u_i)_ε(v + h) − (u_i)_ε(v) = ∫_0^1 ∇(u_i)_ε(v + th)·h dt, so by Tonelli and translation invariance of L^m (B_R + th ⊆ B_{R+1}), ∫_{B_R}|(u_i)_ε(v + h) − (u_i)_ε(v)| dv ≤ |h|·∫_0^1∫_{B_{R+1}}|∇(u_i)_ε| dt ≤ c(R + 2)|h| by step 3. Moreover ∫_{B_R}|u_i(v + h) − (u_i)_ε(v + h)| dv ≤ ‖u_i − (u_i)_ε‖_{1,B_{R+1}} and ∫_{B_R}|(u_i)_ε − u_i| ≤ ‖(u_i)_ε − u_i‖_{1,B_{R+1}}; both tend to 0 as ε → 0 by step 2. The triangle inequality gives the claim.

5. (Cube averages.) Fix R ≥ 1 and δ ∈ (0, 1/√m]. Let 𝒬 = 𝒬(R, δ) be the finite family of half-open cubes Q = δ(z + [0, 1)^m), z ∈ ℤ^m, that meet B_R; they are pairwise disjoint, cover B_R, and lie in B_{R+1} (diam Q = √m·δ ≤ 1). For i ≥ i_{R+3} put a_{i,Q} := δ^{−m}∫_Q u_i ∈ [0, 1] and Au_i := Σ_{Q∈𝒬} a_{i,Q}·1_Q. For v ∈ Q, |u_i(v) − a_{i,Q}| ≤ δ^{−m}∫_Q|u_i(v) − u_i(v')| dv'. Substituting v' = v + h (h ∈ Q − v ⊆ closedBall(0, √mδ)) and using Tonelli and step 4 on B_{R+1}:
 ‖u_i − Au_i‖_{1,B_R} ≤ δ^{−m}Σ_Q∫_Q∫_Q|u_i(v) − u_i(v')| dv' dv ≤ δ^{−m}∫_{|h|≤√mδ}∫_{B_{R+1}}|u_i(v + h) − u_i(v)| dv dh ≤ δ^{−m}·L^m(closedBall(0, √mδ))·c(R + 3)√mδ = C_m·c(R + 3)·δ,
with C_m := L^m(closedBall(0, 1))·m^{(m+1)/2}.

6. (A subsequence that is Cauchy in every L¹(B_R).) Put δ_l := 1/(l√m) for l ≥ 1 and enumerate the countably many pairs (R, l) ∈ ℕ × ℕ with R, l ≥ 1. For each pair the finitely many averages (a_{i,Q})_{Q∈𝒬(R,δ_l)} lie in the compact cube [0, 1]^{𝒬(R,δ_l)}, so every subsequence has a further subsequence along which they converge (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). A diagonal argument gives a strictly increasing σ₀ such that, for every pair (R, l), a_{σ₀(i),Q} converges as i → ∞ for every Q ∈ 𝒬(R, δ_l). (Equivalently, with a single extraction: the averages δ_l^{−m}∫_{δ_l(z+[0,1)^m)} u_i, indexed by the countable set of pairs (l, z) with l ≥ 1 and z ∈ ℤ^m, form a sequence in the compact metrizable product [0, 1]^{ℕ×ℤ^m} (isCompact_univ_pi), and IsCompact.tendsto_subseq gives σ₀ along which all of them converge.) Fix R ∈ ℕ, R ≥ 1. For every l and all large i, i':
 ‖u_{σ₀(i)} − u_{σ₀(i')}‖_{1,B_R} ≤ 2C_m·c(R + 3)·δ_l + Σ_{Q∈𝒬(R,δ_l)}|a_{σ₀(i),Q} − a_{σ₀(i'),Q}|·δ_l^m,
and the sum tends to 0 as i, i' → ∞. Hence limsup_{i,i'→∞}‖u_{σ₀(i)} − u_{σ₀(i')}‖_{1,B_R} ≤ 2C_m·c(R + 3)·δ_l for every l, so (u_{σ₀(i)}) is Cauchy in L¹(B_R) for every R ∈ ℕ.

7. (Almost everywhere convergence.) By step 6, choose inductively j_0 < j_1 < j_2 < … with ‖u_{σ₀(i)} − u_{σ₀(i')}‖_{1,B_{l+1}} ≤ 2^{−l} for all i, i' ≥ j_l, and put σ(l) := σ₀(j_l) for l ∈ ℕ, a strictly increasing map ℕ → ℕ. Fix R ∈ ℕ with R ≥ 1. For l ≥ R − 1 we have B_R ⊆ B_{l+1} and j_{l+1} > j_l, so ∫_{B_R}|u_{σ(l+1)} − u_{σ(l)}| ≤ 2^{−l}; each of the finitely many terms with l < R − 1 is at most L^m(B_R) < ∞. Hence Σ_l∫_{B_R}|u_{σ(l+1)} − u_{σ(l)}| < ∞, and by monotone convergence (lintegral_tsum) Σ_l|u_{σ(l+1)}(v) − u_{σ(l)}(v)| < ∞ for a.e. v ∈ B_R; as ℝ^m = ⋃_{R≥1}B_R, this holds for a.e. v ∈ ℝ^m. Since every u_{σ(l)}(v) is 0 or 1, every nonzero term of this series equals 1; so for a.e. v only finitely many terms are nonzero and the sequence (u_{σ(l)}(v))_l is eventually constant.

8. (The limit set.) Put F' := {v : v ∈ F_{σ(l)} for all large l} = ⋃_{l₀}⋂_{l≥l₀}F_{σ(l)}, a measurable set. At every v where (u_{σ(l)}(v)) is eventually constant, its eventual value is 1_{F'}(v). Hence u_{σ(l)} → 1_{F'} a.e., and |u_{σ(l)} − 1_{F'}| ≤ 1. For R > 0, dominated convergence on B_R (a set of finite measure) gives L^m((F_{σ(l)} Δ F') ∩ B_R) = ∫_{B_R}|u_{σ(l)} − 1_{F'}| dL^m → 0; for R ≤ 0, B_R = ∅. This proves the statement with σ and F'. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mollifier ρ := (∫b)^{−1}b from an even ContDiffBump b with radii 1/2 and 1 (tsupport ρ = closedBall(0, 1), so ρ_ε vanishes outside closedBall(0, ε)); mollified indicators satisfy ∫_{B_{R+1}}|∇(u_i)_ε| ≤ c(R + 2): integrate by parts and test the hypothesis with the mollified field ρ_ε ⋆ ψ, whose tsupport lies in closedBall(0, R + 1 + ε) ⊆ B_{R+2}.
Translation estimate ‖u_i(· + h) − u_i‖_{L¹(B_R)} ≤ c(R + 2)|h| (fundamental theorem of calculus for (u_i)_ε, then ε → 0 by L¹ convergence of mollifications).
Cube averages approximate u_i in L¹(B_R) up to C_m·c(R + 3)·δ; finitely many averages in [0, 1] have convergent subsequences, and a diagonal argument makes (u_{σ₀(i)}) Cauchy in every L¹(B_R).
A fast Cauchy subsequence converges a.e. and is eventually constant a.e.; F' := liminf F_{σ(l)} is measurable and dominated convergence gives L^m((F_{σ(l)} Δ F') ∩ B_R) → 0.

subproblem.title: Area formula for C¹ graphs over an m-plane (Simon Ch. 2, 3.1–3.3)
subproblem.statement: Let m, k ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{m+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, let D ⊆ ℝ^m be open, g : ℝ^m → ℝ^k a map that is C¹ on D, A ⊆ D a measurable set and f : ℝ^{m+k} → ℝ an arbitrary function. Put G(w) := ιw + ι'g(w) and J(w) := √det(DG(w)*∘DG(w)) (DG(w) = fderiv ℝ G w, DG(w)* its adjoint). Then ∫_{G(A)} f dH^m = ∫_A J(w)·f(G(w)) dw, where H^m = μHE[m] on ℝ^{m+k}, dw is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m, and both sides are Bochner integrals (a non-integrable function has integral 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (ι : Euclid m →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (m + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (m + k)) (g : Euclid m → Euclid k) (D A : Set (Euclid m)) (f : Euclid (m + k) → ℝ), (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → IsOpen D → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g D → MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ D → ∫ y in (fun w => ι w + ι' (g w)) '' A, f y ∂μHE[m] = ∫ w in A, Real.sqrt (((fderiv ℝ (fun w => ι w + ι' (g w)) w).adjoint ∘L fderiv ℝ (fun w => ι w + ι' (g w)) w).det) * f (ι w + ι' (g w))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, §3: the linear area formula 3.1 and the area formula 3.2–3.3 for 1:1 Lipschitz maps, obtained "by an approximation argument based on the linear case 3.1" (chapter-02.txt lines 743–776). It is the area formula for the injective C¹ maps G_i used in step 7(a) of the supplied proof of the parent node. The SimonGMT area formula (Chapter02.AreaFormula, Chapter02.WeightedArea) is outside the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so the approximation argument is written out here for C¹ graphs. No sibling child is used.

Notation. ℝ^d = Euclid d. H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^{m+k}; on ℝ^m, μHE[m] is Lebesgue measure L^m (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); μHE[m] is a constant multiple of μH[m] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). ι*, ι'* are the adjoints; ι*ι = id, ι'*ι' = id, ι*ι' = 0, ι'*ι = 0 (isometry and orthogonality). "Borel" means measurable.

1. (Elementary facts.)
(i) ι*G(w) = w for all w. Hence G is injective on ℝ^m and |w − w'| = |ι*(G(w) − G(w'))| ≤ |G(w) − G(w')|.
(ii) For a linear B : ℝ^m → ℝ^k let L_B := ι + ι'B. Then |L_Bh|² = |h|² + |Bh|² ≥ |h|², L_B*L_B = id + B*B, and det(L_B*L_B) = det(id + B*B) ≥ 1 because id + B*B is self-adjoint with all eigenvalues ≥ 1.
(iii) For w ∈ D, g is differentiable at w (D is open and g is C¹ on D), and DG(w) = ι + ι'Dg(w) = L_{Dg(w)}; so J(w) ≥ 1 on D. J is continuous on D, since Dg is continuous on D (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen) and B ↦ √det(id + B*B) is continuous. J is a Borel function on ℝ^m (fderiv is measurable, measurable_fderiv; det and √ are continuous).
(iv) For Borel A' ⊆ D, G(A') is Borel, because G is continuous and injective on D ⊇ A' (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).

2. (Linear area formula, Simon 3.1.) Let L : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+k} be linear and injective. Then H^m(L(A')) = √det(L*L)·L^m(A') for every A' ⊆ ℝ^m. Proof: range L has dimension m; choose a linear isometry κ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+k} with range κ = range L (from an orthonormal basis of range L) and put M := κ*L : ℝ^m → ℝ^m. κκ* is the orthogonal projection onto range κ = range L, so κM = L. Since κ is an isometry, H^m(κ(S)) = μHE[m](S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^m (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and μHE[m] = L^m on ℝ^m; so H^m(L(A')) = L^m(M(A')) = |det M|·L^m(A') (Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap). Finally L*L = M*κ*κM = M*M, so det(L*L) = (det M)² and |det M| = √det(L*L).

3. (Local comparison.) Fix ε ∈ (0, 1/2) and w₀ ∈ D; put B₀ := Dg(w₀) and L₀ := DG(w₀) = ι + ι'B₀. Choose r = r(w₀) > 0 such that ball(w₀, r) ⊆ D, ‖Dg(w) − B₀‖ ≤ ε and (1 − ε)J(w₀) ≤ J(w) ≤ (1 + ε)J(w₀) for all w ∈ ball(w₀, r) (continuity of Dg and of J at w₀).
(a) For w, w' ∈ ball(w₀, r) the map w ↦ g(w) − B₀w has derivative of norm ≤ ε on the convex ball, so |g(w) − g(w') − B₀(w − w')| ≤ ε|w − w'| (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le). As G(w) − G(w') = L₀(w − w') + ι'(g(w) − g(w') − B₀(w − w')) and |w − w'| ≤ |L₀(w − w')| (fact (ii)):
 (1 − ε)|L₀(w − w')| ≤ |G(w) − G(w')| ≤ (1 + ε)|L₀(w − w')|.
(b) Let A' ⊆ ball(w₀, r) be Borel. L₀ is injective, and by (a) the map L₀(A') → G(A'), L₀h ↦ G(h), is (1 + ε)-Lipschitz, while its inverse G(h) ↦ L₀h is (1 − ε)^{−1}-Lipschitz. A Lipschitz map multiplies m-dimensional Hausdorff measure by at most Lip^m (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le; μHE[m] is a multiple of μH[m]). Hence (1 − ε)^m H^m(L₀(A')) ≤ H^m(G(A')) ≤ (1 + ε)^m H^m(L₀(A')), and by step 2, H^m(L₀(A')) = J(w₀)L^m(A'):
 (1 − ε)^m J(w₀) L^m(A') ≤ H^m(G(A')) ≤ (1 + ε)^m J(w₀) L^m(A').
(c) By the choice of r, (1 − ε)J(w₀)L^m(A') ≤ ∫_{A'} J dL^m ≤ (1 + ε)J(w₀)L^m(A'). With c_ε := (1 + ε)^m(1 − ε)^{−(m+1)}, so that (1 + ε)^m/(1 − ε) ≤ c_ε and c_ε^{−1} ≤ (1 − ε)^m/(1 + ε), (b) and (c) give
 c_ε^{−1}·∫_{A'} J dL^m ≤ H^m(G(A')) ≤ c_ε·∫_{A'} J dL^m.

4. (Countable decomposition; the identity on D.) Fix ε. The balls ball(w₀, r(w₀)) of step 3 (w₀ ∈ D) cover D; ℝ^m is second countable, so countably many of them, B_1, B_2, …, cover D (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). For a Borel A' ⊆ D put A'_j := (A' ∩ B_j) ∖ (B_1 ∪ … ∪ B_{j−1}). These sets are Borel, pairwise disjoint, have union A', and each lies in one ball of step 3. G is injective, so G(A') is the disjoint union of the Borel sets G(A'_j) (fact (iv)). Summing the inequality of 3(c) over j (countable additivity of H^m and of B ↦ ∫_B J dL^m) gives c_ε^{−1}∫_{A'} J dL^m ≤ H^m(G(A')) ≤ c_ε∫_{A'} J dL^m in [0, ∞]. Letting ε → 0 (c_ε → 1): H^m(G(A')) = ∫_{A'} J dL^m for every Borel A' ⊆ D.

5. (Push-forward form.) Let ν be the measure on ℝ^m with density J ≥ 0 with respect to L^m⌞A, ν(B) = ∫_{A∩B} J dL^m. For Borel Y ⊆ ℝ^{m+k} the set A ∩ G^{−1}(Y) is Borel (G is continuous on the open D ⊇ A), and Y ∩ G(A) = G(A ∩ G^{−1}(Y)) because G is injective. By step 4, (H^m⌞G(A))(Y) = H^m(G(A ∩ G^{−1}(Y))) = ∫_{A∩G^{−1}(Y)} J dL^m = ν(G^{−1}(Y)) = (G_#ν)(Y). Hence H^m⌞G(A) = G_#ν.

6. (Integrals.) Let f : ℝ^{m+k} → ℝ be arbitrary. ν is concentrated on A, G is continuous and injective on A, and ι* is a continuous left inverse of G; so G restricted to A is a measurable isomorphism onto the Borel set G(A), and ∫ f d(G_#ν) = ∫ f∘G dν for every f, measurable or not (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map for the measurable embedding of the subtype A into ℝ^{m+k}; equivalently: f∘G∘ι* = f on G(A), so f is G_#ν-a.e. strongly measurable iff f∘G is ν-a.e. strongly measurable, and if neither holds both integrals are 0). Moreover ∫ h dν = ∫_A J·h dL^m for every h, because ν has the Borel density J ≥ 0 on A (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul). Therefore
 ∫_{G(A)} f dH^m = ∫ f d(G_#ν) = ∫_A J(w)·f(G(w)) dw,
which is the claim, with J(w) = √det(DG(w)*DG(w)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Linear area formula: H^m(L(A')) = √det(L*L)·L^m(A') via an isometry onto range L and Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap.
Near w₀ the graph map G is (1 ± ε)-bi-Lipschitz relative to its linearization DG(w₀), so H^m(G(A')) = J(w₀)L^m(A') up to factors (1 ± ε)^m, while J varies by at most a factor 1 ± ε.
A countable disjoint decomposition into such pieces, injectivity of G and ε → 0 give H^m(G(A')) = ∫_{A'} J for every Borel A' ⊆ D.
Hence H^m⌞G(A) = G_#(J·L^m⌞A), and the continuous left inverse ι* gives the Bochner identity for every f.

subproblem.title: Affine (n+1)-planes with a constant unit orientation are in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P (Lemma A-plane)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace, let ξ ∈ Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P (n+1)) be a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_0, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P with span{τ_0, …, τ_n} = Q such that ξ(α) = α(τ) for every (n+1)-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every α), and let a ∈ ℝ^P. Put A := {y ∈ ℝ^P : y + a ∈ Q} = Q − a. Then dim Q = n + 1 (Module.finrank ℝ Q = n + 1) and A, oriented by the constant map y ↦ ξ, belongs to class 𝒪 of ℝ^P (InClassO n ℝ^P A (y ↦ ξ)): (i) A is an embedded C² submanifold of dimension n + 1 (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) A); (ii) y ↦ ξ is an orientation of A (IsOrientation (n+1) A (y ↦ ξ): it is continuous on A and for every y ∈ A, ξ is a unit orientation of a subspace that equals tangentSpace A y as a set); (iii) (closure A ∖ A) ∩ ℝ^P = ∅; (iv) A ∩ ℝ^P ≠ ∅.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P (n + 1)) (a : Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → Module.finrank ℝ Q = n + 1 ∧ InClassO n (univ : Set (Euclid P)) {y | y + a ∈ Q} (fun _ => ξ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Lemma A-plane of the supplied proof of the parent node (its steps 1–5), used in the parent's conclusion (step 11); class 𝒪 is Simon 7.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 776–779). No sibling child is used.

Notation. ℝ^d = Euclid d with the Euclidean norm; e_0, …, e_n is the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1} (EuclideanSpace.single j 1). An (n+1)-covector is a continuous alternating (n+1)-linear map (ℝ^P)^{n+1} → ℝ, and α(v) is its value on a family v = (v_0, …, v_n).

1. (Unfolding the hypothesis; dimension.) IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q gives an orthonormal τ : Fin(n+1) → ℝ^P with span{τ_0, …, τ_n} = Q and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(α) = s·α(τ) for every α. An orthonormal family is linearly independent, so τ is a basis of Q with n + 1 elements and Module.finrank ℝ Q = n + 1 (finrank_span_eq_card). This is the first conjunct.

2. (An isometric parametrization.) Define the linear map ι : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, ι(v) := Σ_j v_j·τ_j, and ψ(v) := ι(v) − a. By orthonormality |ι(v)|² = Σ_j v_j² = |v|², so ι is a linear isometry, in particular injective, and its range is span τ = Q.

3. (A = ψ(ℝ^{n+1}).) For y ∈ ℝ^P: y ∈ A ⟺ y + a ∈ Q = range ι ⟺ y + a = ι(v) for some v ⟺ y = ψ(v) for some v.

4. (A is an embedded C² (n+1)-submanifold.) Let y ∈ A. Take V := ℝ^{n+1}, W := ℝ^P (both open, y ∈ W) and the map ψ.
- ψ is affine (a constant plus a continuous linear map), hence C^∞, in particular ContDiffOn ℝ 2 ψ V.
- ψ is injective because ι is; so InjOn ψ V.
- ψ(V) = A = W ∩ A by step 3.
- For every compact K ⊆ W, V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) = ψ^{−1}(K) is closed (ψ is continuous) and bounded: for v ∈ ψ^{−1}(K), |v| = |ι(v)| = |ψ(v) + a| ≤ max_{z∈K}|z| + |a|. By Heine–Borel it is compact.
- The derivative of ψ at every point is ι, which is injective.
These are the clauses of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) A at the point y.

5. (A is closed and nonempty.) Q is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and A is its preimage under the continuous map y ↦ y + a. So A is closed, closure A = A and (closure A ∖ A) ∩ ℝ^P = ∅. Also −a ∈ A because −a + a = 0 ∈ Q, so A ∩ ℝ^P ≠ ∅.

6. (Tangent spaces.) Let y ∈ A. Claim: tangentSpace A y = Q as subsets of ℝ^P.
(⊆) Let v ∈ tangentSpace A y: there is γ : ℝ → ℝ^P, C¹ on (−1, 1), with γ((−1, 1)) ⊆ A, γ(0) = y and HasDerivAt γ v 0. subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, E ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. Let η := η_{y,λ} (dilation y λ, η(z) = λ^{−1}(z − y)) and η_#T := blowUp T y λ ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)). If T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N, H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1]), then η_#T(ω) = ∫_{η(E)} ξ_N(y + λw)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(η(U)), i.e. IsBoundaryOfRegion (blowUp T y λ) (η(E)) (w ↦ ξ_N(y + λw)).

2. (Hypothesis.) IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N applied to ω' gives T(ω') = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω'(z)) dH^{n+1}(z).

3. (Exterior derivative of ω' = ω∘η.) Notation. P := n + 1 + k; ℝ^d = Euclid d; α(Le) := α(Le_0, …, Le_n) for an (n+1)-covector α and a linear L : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P. ι*, ι'* are the adjoints: ι*ι = id, ι'*ι' = id, ι*ι' = 0, ι'*ι = 0, and (orthogonality and spanning) y = ιι*y + ι'ι'*y and |y|² = |ι*y|² + |ι'*y|² for every y. B_R := ball(0, R) ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}; H^{n+1} := μHE[n+1]; L^{n+1} := volume on ℝ^{n+1}; div φ := trace Dφ; G(w) := ιw + ι'b. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, and a form ω is admissible if |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Part A (lifting divergence fields to test forms).
A1. Let Ω be the standard volume form of ℝ^{n+1}, Ω(z_0, …, z_n) := det[z_0 | … | z_n]: the determinant Module.Basis.det of the standard basis, made a continuous alternating map with AlternatingMap.mkContinuous and the Leibniz bound |det[z_0 | … | z_n]| ≤ (n+1)!·∏_j|z_j|. Ω(e_0, …, e_n) = 1, and Ω(z, e_0, …, ê_j, …, e_n) = (−1)^j·z_j for z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and j ≤ n (moving z to position j takes j transpositions).
A2. For a C^∞ compactly supported vector field φ on ℝ^{n+1} let α̃(v) := Ω(φ(v), ·, …, ·) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft), an n-form on ℝ^{n+1}. α̃ is C^∞ (a continuous linear function of φ(v)), tsupport α̃ ⊆ tsupport φ, and by the coordinate formula for d (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply: dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = Σ_j (−1)^j·D[β(·)(e_0, …, ê_j, …, e_n)](v)e_j) together with A1,
 dα̃(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = Σ_j (−1)^j·∂_j((−1)^jφ_j)(v) = Σ_j ∂_jφ_j(v) = div φ(v).
A3. Fix h > 0 and let χ(t) := smoothTransition((4h² − t)/(3h²)) for t ∈ ℝ: χ is C^∞, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ(t) = 1 for t ≤ h² and χ(t) = 0 for t ≥ 4h². Put ζ(y) := χ(|ι'*y|²), a C^∞ function on ℝ^P.
A4. Define ω_φ(y) := ζ(y)·(α̃(ι*y)∘ι*), i.e. ζ times the pull-back affinePullbackForm ι* 0 α̃. ω_φ is C^∞. If ω_φ(y) ≠ 0 then ι*y ∈ tsupport φ and |ι'*y| < 2h; the set {y : ι*y ∈ tsupport φ, |ι'*y| ≤ 2h} is closed and bounded (|y|² = |ι*y|² + |ι'*y|²), hence compact. So ω_φ ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) and tsupport ω_φ ⊆ {ιv + ι'w : v ∈ tsupport φ, |w| ≤ 2h}.
A5. (Uniform comass bound.) z ↦ Ω(z, ·)∘ι* is a linear map from ℝ^{n+1} to n-covectors on ℝ^P, and |·| is continuous and absolutely homogeneous; so K := max(1, sup_{|z|≤1}|Ω(z, ·)∘ι*|) is finite (compact unit ball) and depends only on n, k and ι. If |φ| ≤ 1 everywhere, then |ω_φ(y)| = ζ(y)·|Ω(φ(ι*y), ·)∘ι*| ≤ K for all y.
A6. (Key identity.) Let v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, w ∈ ℝ^k with |w| < h, y₀ := ιv + ι'w, and let L : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be linear with ι*L = id. Then dω_φ(y₀)(Le) = div φ(v). Indeed |ι'*y|² < h² for y near y₀, so ζ = 1 near y₀ and ω_φ coincides near y₀ with π^#α̃ := affinePullbackForm ι* 0 α̃. The exterior derivative at a point depends only on the germ (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so dω_φ(y₀) = d(π^#α̃)(y₀) = dα̃(ι*y₀)∘ι* (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm) = dα̃(v)∘ι*. Hence dω_φ(y₀)(Le_0, …, Le_n) = dα̃(v)(ι*Le_0, …, ι*Le_n) = dα̃(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = div φ(v) by A2.

Part B (uniform perimeter bounds).
B1. Fix R > 0 and put h := |b| + 1, R₂ := R + 2h. Let c₂ be the constant of (H4) for R₂. By (H1), (H2) with ε = 1, (H3) and (H4), all for R₂, there is i₀ such that for i ≥ i₀: g_i is differentiable on B_{R₂}; |g_i(w) − b| < 1, hence |g_i(w)| < h, on B_{R₂}; the representation (H3) holds for every ω supported in ball(0, R₂); and currentEval(S_i)(ω) ≤ c₂ for every admissible ω supported in ball(0, R₂).
B2. Let i ≥ i₀ and let φ be C^∞ with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ B_R and |φ| ≤ 1; let ω := ω_φ with h from B1. For v ∈ tsupport φ and |w| ≤ 2h, |ιv + ι'w| ≤ |v| + |w| < R + 2h, so tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R₂). For w ∈ B_{R₂}: G_i(w) = ιw + ι'g_i(w) with |g_i(w)| < h, g_i is differentiable at w, DG_i(w) = ι + ι'Dg_i(w) and ι*DG_i(w) = id; so by A6, dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e) = div φ(w). Hence by (H3), currentEval(S_i)(ω) = ∫_{F_i∩B_{R₂}} div φ = ∫_{F_i} div φ, because div φ vanishes outside tsupport φ ⊆ B_{R₂} (φ vanishes near such points) and F_i is measurable.
B3. ω/K is admissible (A5) and has the same support as ω, and currentEval(S_i) is linear in the form (tsupport(ω/K) = tsupport ω, so the same branch of currentEval applies, and S_i is linear). By B1, ∫_{F_i} div φ = K·currentEval(S_i)(ω/K) ≤ K·c₂. Thus for every R > 0 there are c(R) := K·c₂ and i₀ such that ∫_{F_i} div φ ≤ c(R) for every i ≥ i₀ and every admissible φ with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R: this is the hypothesis of bv_compactness for the measurable sets F_i ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}.

Part C (compactness).
C1. bv_compactness (with m := n + 1) gives a strictly increasing σ and a measurable F' ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} with L^{n+1}((F_{σ(i)} Δ F') ∩ B_R) → 0 for every R.

Part D (identification of S).
D1. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P). tsupport ω is compact, so tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R) for some R > 0. Put h_i(w) := dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e) and h(w) := dω(G(w))(ιe). dω is continuous with compact support, hence bounded, say by M, and uniformly continuous.
D2. By (H1)–(H2) (and |ι'u| = |u|), for every ε > 0 and all large i, |G_i(w) − G(w)| = |g_i(w) − b| < ε and ‖DG_i(w) − ι‖ = ‖Dg_i(w)‖ < ε for all w ∈ B_R. The map (y, L) ↦ dω(y)(Le) is uniformly continuous on ℝ^P × {L : ‖L‖ ≤ 2}, because dω is uniformly continuous and bounded and α is multilinear: |α(z) − α'(z')| ≤ ‖α − α'‖·∏_j|z_j| + ‖α'‖·Σ_j|z_j − z'_j|·∏_{l≠j}max(|z_l|, |z'_l|). Hence sup_{B_R}|h_i − h| → 0, and |h_i| ≤ M' := 2^{n+1}M on B_R for all large i.
D3. For large i, h_i is measurable on B_R: G_i is continuous on B_R and w ↦ DG_i(w) = ι + ι'Dg_i(w) is measurable (measurable_fderiv); h is continuous.
D4. By (H3), for all large i, currentEval(S_{σ(i)})(ω) = ∫_{F_{σ(i)}∩B_R} h_{σ(i)}, and
 |∫_{F_{σ(i)}∩B_R} h_{σ(i)} − ∫_{F'∩B_R} h| ≤ ∫_{B_R}|1_{F_{σ(i)}} − 1_{F'}|·|h_{σ(i)}| + ∫_{F'∩B_R}|h_{σ(i)} − h| ≤ M'·L^{n+1}((F_{σ(i)} Δ F') ∩ B_R) + L^{n+1}(B_R)·sup_{B_R}|h_{σ(i)} − h|,
which tends to 0 by C1 and D2.
D5. S_i ⇀ S gives currentEval(S_{σ(i)})(ω) → S(ω). Hence S(ω) = ∫_{F'∩B_R} h = ∫_{F'} h, because for |w| ≥ R, |G(w)|² = |w|² + |b|² ≥ R², so G(w) ∉ ball(0, R) ⊇ tsupport ω ⊇ tsupport dω and h(w) = 0.

Part E (transfer to the plane).
E1. G is an isometry of ℝ^{n+1} onto A_b := {ιw + ι'b : w ∈ ℝ^{n+1}} (|G(w) − G(w')| = |w − w'|), hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). F := G(F') is measurable and F ⊆ A_b = {y : ∃ w, y = ιw + ι'b}.
E2. Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries: G_#(μHE[n+1] on ℝ^{n+1}) = H^{n+1}⌞range G (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), and μHE[n+1] = L^{n+1} on ℝ^{n+1} (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). As G is injective, H^{n+1}⌞F = G_#(L^{n+1}⌞F') and ∫_F f dH^{n+1} = ∫_{F'} f(G(w)) dw for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
E3. With f(y) := ξ_A(dω(y)) and ξ_A(α) = α(ιe): ∫_F ξ_A(dω(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) = ∫_{F'} dω(G(w))(ιe) dw = ∫_{F'} h = S(ω) by D5. As ω was arbitrary, IsBoundaryOfRegion S F (y ↦ ξ_A), with F measurable and F ⊆ {y : ∃ w, y = ιw + ι'b}. ∎
proof_key_steps: Divergence fields φ on ℝ^{n+1} lift to test forms ω_φ = ζ·(Ω(φ∘ι*, ·)∘ι*) on ℝ^P with |ω_φ| ≤ K, supported in a slab |ι'*y| ≤ 2h, and dω_φ(ιv + ι'w)(Le) = div φ(v) whenever |w| < h and ι*L = id.
By (H2) the graphs G_i = ι + ι'g_i lie in that slab and ι*DG_i = id, so (H3) gives currentEval(S_i)(ω_φ) = ∫_{F_i} div φ, which (H4) bounds by K·c₂: uniform local perimeter bounds.
bv_compactness yields F' with 1_{F_σ(i)} → 1_{F'} in L¹_loc; (H1)–(H2) give uniform convergence of the integrands, so S(ω) = ∫_{F'} dω(ιw + ι'b)(ιe) dw.
The isometry G(w) = ιw + ι'b carries this to S(ω) = ∫_{G(F')} ξ_A(dω) dH^{n+1}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 4, (4a)–(4e), of the supplied proof of the parent node (graph chart of N at x and the orientation formula), written in orthonormal coordinates ι, ι' so that the accepted graph lemma applies. Embedded submanifolds and tangent spaces: Simon Ch. 2, §4 (4.1); orientations: Simon Ch. 6, 2.2. Sibling children used: orientation_sign (Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg) and graph_orientation_jacobian (Submission.dgcr_graph_orientation_jacobian).

Notation. P := n + 1 + k; ℝ^d = Euclid d; e_0, …, e_n the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}; for a linear L : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P and an (n+1)-covector α, α(Le) := α(Le_0, …, Le_n); L* is the adjoint. B_r := ball(0, r) (in ℝ^{n+1} or ℝ^k, as indicated). If ι : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^P are linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, then ι*ι = id, ι'*ι' = id, ι*ι' = 0 and ι'*ι = 0 (e.g. ⟨ι*ιv, v'⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιv'⟩ = ⟨v, v'⟩); if moreover every y is ιv + ι'w, then v = ι*y and w = ι'*y, so y = ιι*y + ι'ι'*y and |y|² = |ι*y|² + |ι'*y|².

1. (The tangent plane at x.) IsOrientation (n+1) N ξ_N at x ∈ N gives a subspace Q₀ with (Q₀ : Set) = tangentSpace N x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_N(x)) Q₀. The orthonormal family in IsUnitOrientationOf has n + 1 vectors and spans Q₀, so dim Q₀ = n + 1, and dim Q₀^⊥ = P − (n + 1) = k (Submodule.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal).

2. (Orthonormal coordinates.) Choose orthonormal bases of Q₀ and of Q₀^⊥ indexed by Fin(n+1) and Fin k (stdOrthonormalBasis, reindexed by the dimensions of step 1), and let ι₀ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be the corresponding linear isometries v ↦ Σ_j v_j·(basis vector j). Then range ι₀ = Q₀, range ι' = Q₀^⊥, ⟨ι₀v, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, and every y equals proj_{Q₀}y + proj_{Q₀^⊥}y, which has the form ι₀v + ι'w.

3. (An orientation-compatible ι.) τ₀ := (ι₀e_0, …, ι₀e_n) is orthonormal with span Q₀, so ζ₀(α) := α(τ₀) is a unit orientation of Q₀. By orientation_sign, ξ_N(x) = ζ₀ or ξ_N(x) = −ζ₀. In the first case put ι := ι₀. In the second, let ρ be the linear isometry of ℝ^{n+1} that negates coordinate 0 and fixes the others, and put ι := ι₀∘ρ; then ιe_0 = −ι₀e_0 and ιe_j = ι₀e_j for j ≥ 1, so α(ιe) = −α(τ₀) by multilinearity. In both cases ι is a linear isometry with range Q₀, ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0, every y is ιv + ι'w, and ξ_N(x)(α) = α(ιe) for every α. This proves (a) and (d).

4. (A chart at x.) IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N at x gives an open V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, an open W ∋ x and ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P such that ψ is C² on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) is injective for every z ∈ V. Choose z₀ ∈ V with ψ(z₀) = x.

5. (range Dψ(z₀) = Q₀.) Let h ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and choose ε > 0 with z₀ + εth ∈ V for |t| < 1 (V is open). Then γ(t) := ψ(z₀ + εth) is C¹ on (−1, 1), takes values in ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = x and γ'(0) = εDψ(z₀)h. So εDψ(z₀)h ∈ tangentSpace N x = Q₀ and Dψ(z₀)h ∈ Q₀. Thus range Dψ(z₀) ⊆ Q₀, and both have dimension n + 1 (Dψ(z₀) is injective), so range Dψ(z₀) = Q₀ = range ι.

6. (Inverse function theorem.) Put Φ(z) := ι*(ψ(z) − x). Φ is C² on V, Φ(z₀) = 0 and DΦ(z) = ι*Dψ(z). DΦ(z₀) is injective: if ι*Dψ(z₀)h = 0, write Dψ(z₀)h = ιv (step 5); then v = ι*ιv = 0, so Dψ(z₀)h = 0 and h = 0. Hence DΦ(z₀) is a linear automorphism of ℝ^{n+1}. DΦ is continuous on V and invertibility is an open condition, so there is an open V₁ with z₀ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V on which every DΦ(z) is invertible. Φ is C¹ at z₀, so it has strict derivative DΦ(z₀) there (ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt), and the inverse function theorem (HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, after shrinking the source into V₁) gives an open V₀ with z₀ ∈ V₀ ⊆ V₁ such that Φ maps V₀ homeomorphically onto an open set O ∋ 0, with inverse χ : O → V₀. At every a ∈ O, Φ is C² at χ(a) with invertible derivative, so χ is C² at a (OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm); in particular χ is C¹ on O.

7. (The graph function.) Define u(v) := ι'*(ψ(χ(v)) − x) for v ∈ O (and u(v) := 0 for v ∉ O). Then u is C¹ on O, u(0) = ι'*(ψ(z₀) − x) = 0, and Du(0) = ι'*Dψ(z₀)Dχ(0) = 0 because range Dψ(z₀) = range ι and ι'*ι = 0. For v ∈ O the decomposition y = ιι*y + ι'ι'*y gives ψ(χ(v)) − x = ιΦ(χ(v)) + ι'u(v) = ιv + ι'u(v). Writing Γ(v) := x + ιv + ι'u(v), we get Γ(v) = ψ(χ(v)) ∈ N for every v ∈ O.

8. (Near x, N is covered by ψ(V₀).) The set C := ψ(V ∖ V₀) is relatively closed in W. Indeed, let y ∈ W and c_j ∈ V ∖ V₀ with ψ(c_j) → y. Choose r > 0 with K := closedBall(y, r) ⊆ W. For large j, ψ(c_j) ∈ K, so c_j lies in the compact set V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K), and a subsequence converges to some c ∈ V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). Since V₀ is open, V ∖ V₀ is closed in V, so c ∈ V ∖ V₀; ψ is continuous at c, so y = ψ(c) ∈ C. As ψ is injective on V and x = ψ(z₀) with z₀ ∈ V₀, x ∉ C. Hence there is s > 0 with ball(x, s) ⊆ W and ball(x, s) ∩ C = ∅, and then N ∩ ball(x, s) ⊆ (W ∩ N) ∖ C = ψ(V) ∖ ψ(V ∖ V₀) ⊆ ψ(V₀).

9. (Radii; conclusion (b).) Put δ₂ := s/2. As u is continuous at 0 with u(0) = 0 and O is an open neighbourhood of 0, choose δ₁ ∈ (0, s/2] with B_{δ₁} ⊆ O and |u(v)| < δ₂ for v ∈ B_{δ₁}. Then u is C¹ on B_{δ₁}, u(0) = 0, fderiv ℝ u 0 = 0 (0 is an interior point of O, where u is differentiable with derivative 0) and u(B_{δ₁}) ⊆ B_{δ₂}: this is (b). Every point of the cylinder Z := {x + ιv + ι'w : v ∈ B_{δ₁}, w ∈ B_{δ₂}} satisfies |ιv + ι'w|² = |v|² + |w|² < δ₁² + δ₂² < s², so Z ⊆ ball(x, s).

10. (N ∩ Z = Γ(B_{δ₁}); conclusion (c).) (⊇) For v ∈ B_{δ₁}, Γ(v) ∈ N by step 7, and Γ(v) = x + ιv + ι'u(v) with |u(v)| < δ₂, so Γ(v) ∈ Z. (⊆) Let y ∈ N ∩ Z, y = x + ιv' + ι'w' with |v'| < δ₁ and |w'| < δ₂. By steps 8–9, y ∈ N ∩ ball(x, s) ⊆ ψ(V₀), so y = ψ(z) with z ∈ V₀. Then Φ(z) = ι*(y − x) = ι*(ιv' + ι'w') = v', so v' ∈ O and z = χ(v'); hence y = ψ(χ(v')) = Γ(v') with v' ∈ B_{δ₁}.

11. (Tangent planes along the graph.) Fix v ∈ B_{δ₁}. u is differentiable at v, DΓ(v) = ι + ι'Du(v) and ι*DΓ(v) = id, so DΓ(v) is injective and range DΓ(v) has dimension n + 1. For h ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and small ε > 0, t ↦ Γ(v + εth) (t ∈ (−1, 1)) is C¹, takes values in Γ(B_{δ₁}) ⊆ N and has velocity εDΓ(v)h at t = 0. IsOrientation at Γ(v) ∈ N gives a subspace Q_v with (Q_v : Set) = tangentSpace N (Γ(v)) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_N(Γ(v))) Q_v, and dim Q_v = n + 1 as in step 1. Hence DΓ(v)h ∈ Q_v for every h, range DΓ(v) ⊆ Q_v, and range DΓ(v) = Q_v by dimension.

12. (Two unit orientations along the graph.) Apply graph_orientation_jacobian with n + 1 in place of n (n + 1 > 0), z := x, s := δ₁ and u (C¹ on B_{δ₁}, orthogonality from (a)): there are ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and β : ℝ^P → Λ^{n+1}(ℝ^P), both continuous on Σ := Γ(B_{δ₁}), with ξ(y)(β(y)) = 1 for y ∈ Σ, ξ(Γ(v)) a unit orientation of range DΓ(v), and α(DΓ(v)e) = J(v)·ξ(Γ(v))(α) for all v ∈ B_{δ₁} and all α, where J(v) := √det(DΓ(v)*DΓ(v)). By step 11 and orientation_sign, for each v ∈ B_{δ₁} either ξ_N(Γ(v)) = ξ(Γ(v)) or ξ_N(Γ(v)) = −ξ(Γ(v)). Put s(v) := ξ_N(Γ(v))(β(Γ(v))); then s(v) = 1 in the first case and s(v) = −1 in the second.

13. (The sign is constant.) s is continuous on B_{δ₁}: Γ is continuous on B_{δ₁} with values in Σ ⊆ N, ξ_N is continuous on N (IsOrientation), β is continuous on Σ, and evaluation (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α) is continuous. B_{δ₁} is connected (convex, hence preconnected), and s maps it into the finite, hence discrete, set {1, −1}, so s is constant (IsPreconnected.constant_of_mapsTo with Set.Finite.isDiscrete).

14. (s(0) = 1.) Γ(0) = x since u(0) = 0. DΓ(0) = ι + ι'Du(0) = ι, so DΓ(0)*DΓ(0) = ι*ι = id and J(0) = √1 = 1. The identity of step 12 at v = 0 gives ξ(x)(α) = α(ιe) = ξ_N(x)(α) for every α (step 3), i.e. ξ(x) = ξ_N(x), so s(0) = ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1.

15. (Conclusion (e).) By steps 13–14, s(v) = 1 for every v ∈ B_{δ₁}, which excludes ξ_N(Γ(v)) = −ξ(Γ(v)) (that would give s(v) = −ξ(Γ(v))(β(Γ(v))) = −1). Hence ξ_N(Γ(v)) = ξ(Γ(v)), and the identity of step 12 becomes α(DΓ(v)e) = √det(DΓ(v)*DΓ(v))·ξ_N(Γ(v))(α) for every v ∈ B_{δ₁} and every α. With steps 3, 9 and 10 all conclusions (a)–(e) hold. ∎

subproblem.title: Nonzero zero-scale limits force the blow-up centres to lie within O(λ_i) of N, and x ∈ N (parent step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, N, E ⊆ ℝ^P, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝ^P, points x_i ∈ ℝ^P and scales λ_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ), and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, E ⊆ N, T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N), x ∈ U, x_i → x, λ_i → 0, the blow-ups η_{x_i,λ_i#}T (blowUp T x_i λ_i) converge weakly to S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(η_{x_i,λ_i#}T)(ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P)), and spt S ≠ ∅. Then x ∈ N, and there is C₀ > 0 such that for every i some p ∈ N satisfies |p − x_i| ≤ C₀λ_i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U N E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ i, 0 < lams i) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → E ⊆ N → IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → x ∈ U → Tendsto xs atTop (𝓝 x) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ConvergesWeakly (fun i => blowUp T (xs i) (lams i) (hlams i).ne') S → S.support.Nonempty → x ∈ N ∧ ∃ C₀ : ℝ, 0 < C₀ ∧ ∀ i, ∃ p ∈ N, dist p (xs i) ≤ C₀ * lams i
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 3 of the supplied proof of the parent node ("dist(x_i, N) = O(λ_i), and x ∈ N"), together with the last bullet of its step 1 (S_i(ω) = 0 when tsupport ω misses η_i(N)). Support of a current: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (chapter-06.txt line 299). Sibling child used: blowup_region (Submission.codim1_zsl_blowUp_isBoundaryOfRegion).

Notation. η_i := dilation x_i λ_i (η_i(z) = λ_i^{−1}(z − x_i)), S_i := blowUp T x_i λ_i ∈ 𝒟_n(η_i(U)), H^{n+1} := μHE[n+1]. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω) if tsupport ω ⊆ η_i(U) and 0 otherwise. Hypothesis (b) says currentEval(S_i)(ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P). infDist(z, B) is Metric.infDist.

1. (Vanishing away from η_i(N).) Let i ∈ ℕ and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ∩ η_i(N) = ∅. Then currentEval(S_i)(ω) = 0. If tsupport ω ⊄ η_i(U) this is the definition of currentEval. Otherwise currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω) = ∫_{η_i(E)} ξ_N(x_i + λ_iw)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w) by blowup_region (y := x_i, λ := λ_i). For w ∈ η_i(E) ⊆ η_i(N) we have w ∉ tsupport ω; since tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), dω(w) = 0 and the integrand vanishes at w. A set integral of a function vanishing on the set is 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero; no measurability is needed).

2. (Distance criterion.) Let R ≥ 0 and i be such that |p − x_i| > λ_iR for every p ∈ N. Then closedBall(0, R) ∩ η_i(N) = ∅, because |η_i(p)| = |p − x_i|/λ_i > R for p ∈ N.

3. (A criterion for S = 0.) Suppose σ : ℕ → ℕ is strictly increasing and, for every R ≥ 0, there is j₀ such that for all j ≥ j₀ every p ∈ N satisfies |p − x_{σ(j)}| > λ_{σ(j)}R. Then S(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P): tsupport ω is compact, so tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R ≥ 0; by steps 2 and 1, currentEval(S_{σ(j)})(ω) = 0 for all j ≥ j₀; and currentEval(S_{σ(j)})(ω) → S(ω) by (b) composed with σ (σ(j) → ∞).

4. (S = 0 contradicts spt S ≠ ∅.) If S(ω) = 0 for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), then spt S = ∅: for z ∈ ℝ^P the open ball W := ball(z, 1) has compact closure closedBall(z, 1) ⊆ ℝ^P and S vanishes on W, so z ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion S and z ∉ spt S = ℝ^P ∖ zeroRegion S. This contradicts spt S ≠ ∅. Hence the situation of step 3 never occurs.

5. (N ≠ ∅.) If N = ∅, the condition of step 3 holds vacuously with σ = id, contradicting step 4. So N ≠ ∅, and infDist(·, N) is a finite 1-Lipschitz function.

6. (The rescaled distances are bounded.) Put r_i := infDist(x_i, N)/λ_i ≥ 0. Claim: (r_i) is bounded above. Otherwise, for every j ∈ ℕ there are infinitely many i with r_i > j (if only finitely many i had r_i > j, then r would be bounded by the maximum of j and these finitely many values). By Filter.extraction_forall_of_frequently there is a strictly increasing σ with r_{σ(j)} > j for every j. For R ≥ 0 and j > R every p ∈ N then satisfies |p − x_{σ(j)}| ≥ infDist(x_{σ(j)}, N) = λ_{σ(j)}r_{σ(j)} > λ_{σ(j)}R, so the condition of step 3 holds, contradicting step 4. Hence there is M ≥ 0 with infDist(x_i, N) ≤ Mλ_i for every i.

7. (The constant C₀.) Put C₀ := M + 1 > 0. For each i, infDist(x_i, N) ≤ Mλ_i < C₀λ_i (λ_i > 0), so by Metric.infDist_lt_iff (N ≠ ∅) there is p ∈ N with |p − x_i| < C₀λ_i; in particular dist(p, x_i) ≤ C₀λ_i.

8. (x ∈ N.) For every i, infDist(x, N) ≤ |x − x_i| + infDist(x_i, N) ≤ |x − x_i| + Mλ_i, and the right side tends to 0 (x_i → x, λ_i → 0). So infDist(x, N) = 0 and x ∈ closure N (Metric.mem_closure_iff_infDist_zero, N ≠ ∅). Since x ∈ U and (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, x ∈ N. ∎
proof_key_steps: By blowup_region, currentEval(S_i)(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω misses η_i(N), since dω vanishes on η_i(E) ⊆ η_i(N).
If infDist(x_i, N)/λ_i were unbounded, along a subsequence every compactly supported ω would eventually miss η_i(N); then S = 0 and spt S = ∅, a contradiction (this also forces N ≠ ∅).
Hence infDist(x_i, N) ≤ Mλ_i, giving p_i ∈ N with |p_i − x_i| ≤ (M + 1)λ_i, and infDist(x, N) = 0 gives x ∈ closure N ∩ U ⊆ N.

Assume: U is open; E is measurable and E ⊆ N; T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(y)(dω(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N); x ∈ U; x_i → x; λ_i → 0; (a) there are C ∈ ℝ and r₀ > 0 with M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Cρ^n) (T.massOn (ball y ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C·ρ^n)) for all y ∈ B_{r₀}(x) and 0 < ρ < r₀; (b) the blow-ups η_{x_i,λ_i#}T (blowUp T x_i λ_i) converge weakly to S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (c) for every i there is p ∈ N with |p − x_i| ≤ C₀λ_i; (d) ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, and every y ∈ ℝ^P equals ιv + ι'w for some v, w; (e) δ₁ > 0, δ₂ > 0, u is C¹ on B_{δ₁} := ball(0, δ₁) ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0 and u(B_{δ₁}) ⊆ ball(0, δ₂) ⊆ ℝ^k; (f) with Γ(v) := x + ιv + ι'u(v): N ∩ {x + ιv + ι'w : |v| < δ₁, |w| < δ₂} = Γ(B_{δ₁}); (g) ξ_N(x)(α) = α(ιe_0, …, ιe_n) for every (n+1)-covector α (e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1); (h) for every v ∈ B_{δ₁} and every (n+1)-covector α, α(DΓ(v)e_0, …, DΓ(v)e_n) = √det(DΓ(v)*∘DΓ(v))·ξ_N(Γ(v))(α). subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7(a) of the supplied proof of the parent node written in the coordinates of the graph chart, followed by its steps 7(b)–10 in the form of the sibling child flat_limit. Simon 7.5.3 and 7.5.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 790–901). Departure: the representation of the blow-ups is proved for every test form supported in a ball ball(0, R), using that η_i(N) ∩ ball(0, R) lies on the rescaled graph over B_R (the supplied step 6(c)), instead of in the cylinders C_R; this is the form flat_limit needs. Sibling children used: blowup_region (Submission.codim1_zsl_blowUp_isBoundaryOfRegion), graph_area (Submission.codim1_zsl_graph_area_formula), flat_limit (Submission.codim1_zsl_flat_graph_limit) and testform_corr (Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr).

Notation. P := n + 1 + k; e_0, …, e_n the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}; α(Le) := α(Le_0, …, Le_n). ι*, ι'* are the adjoints: ι*ι = id, ι'*ι' = id, ι*ι' = 0, ι'*ι = 0, y = ιι*y + ι'ι'*y and |y|² = |ι*y|² + |ι'*y|² (by (d)). B_r := ball(0, r) in ℝ^{n+1} (or ℝ^k). Γ(v) := x + ιv + ι'u(v); Z := {x + ιv + ι'w : v ∈ B_{δ₁}, w ∈ B_{δ₂}}. η_i := dilation x_i λ_i, S_i := blowUp T x_i λ_i ∈ 𝒟_n(η_i(U)), H^{n+1} := μHE[n+1]. C, r₀ are the constants of (a) and c_* := max(C, 0). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ω is admissible if |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

0. (Preliminaries.) Z = {y : |ι*(y − x)| < δ₁, |ι'*(y − x)| < δ₂} (by the decomposition of y − x), so Z is open, and x ∈ Z. Du is continuous on the open ball B_{δ₁} (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen) and Du(0) = 0. If C₀ < 0, hypothesis (c) fails for i = 0 (|p − x_0| ≥ 0 > C₀λ_0) and there is nothing to prove; so assume C₀ ≥ 0. For v ∈ B_{δ₁}, u(v) = ι'*(Γ(v) − x), and Γ(v) ∈ N ∩ Z by (f).

1. (Coordinates of the centres.) s_i := ι*(x_i − x), t_i := ι'*(x_i − x); then x_i − x = ιs_i + ι't_i, s_i → 0 and t_i → 0.

2. (Rescaled graphs.) For w ∈ ℝ^{n+1} put g_i(w) := λ_i^{−1}(u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i), G_i(w) := ιw + ι'g_i(w), and D_i := {w : s_i + λ_iw ∈ B_{δ₁}} (open). For every w, λ_iG_i(w) = ι(λ_iw) + ι'(u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i) = Γ(s_i + λ_iw) − x_i, i.e. η_i(Γ(s_i + λ_iw)) = G_i(w) and x_i + λ_iG_i(w) = Γ(s_i + λ_iw). For w ∈ D_i, g_i is differentiable at w with Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) (chain rule; the factors λ_i^{−1} and λ_i cancel), so DG_i(w) = ι + ι'Du(s_i + λ_iw) = DΓ(s_i + λ_iw); and g_i is C¹ on D_i.

3. (Bounded offsets.) For each i choose p_i ∈ N with |p_i − x_i| ≤ C₀λ_i (c). Then p_i → x, so p_i ∈ Z for i ≥ i₁ and, by (f), p_i = Γ(v_i) with v_i ∈ B_{δ₁} and v_i = ι*(p_i − x). Put w_i := (v_i − s_i)/λ_i = ι*(p_i − x_i)/λ_i, so |w_i| ≤ C₀. By step 0, g_i(w_i) = (u(v_i) − t_i)/λ_i = ι'*(p_i − x_i)/λ_i, so |g_i(w_i)| ≤ C₀. Choose ρ₁ ∈ (0, δ₁] with ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ 1 for |v| < ρ₁, and i₂ ≥ i₁ with |s_i| + λ_iC₀ < ρ₁ for all i ≥ i₂. For such i the convex set {w : |s_i + λ_iw| < ρ₁} contains 0 and w_i, and g_i is differentiable on it with ‖Dg_i‖ ≤ 1; by the mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le), |g_i(0)| ≤ |g_i(w_i)| + |w_i| ≤ 2C₀.

4. (The offset b.) The points g_i(0), i ≥ i₂, lie in the compact ball closedBall(0, 2C₀) ⊆ ℝ^k; choose a strictly increasing σ with σ(0) ≥ i₂ and b ∈ ℝ^k with g_{σ(i)}(0) → b (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). Below, a property of the sequence that holds for all large indices j holds for j = σ(i) for all large i, because σ(i) ≥ i.

5. (C¹ convergence: (H1) and (H2) of flat_limit for g_{σ(i)}.) Let R > 0 and ε > 0; put ε' := min(ε, ε/(2R)) and choose ρ ∈ (0, δ₁] with ‖Du(v)‖ < ε' for |v| < ρ. For all large i, |s_{σ(i)}| + λ_{σ(i)}R < ρ and |g_{σ(i)}(0) − b| < ε/2. Then for w ∈ B_R, s_{σ(i)} + λ_{σ(i)}w ∈ B_ρ ⊆ B_{δ₁}, so g_{σ(i)} is differentiable at w with ‖Dg_{σ(i)}(w)‖ < ε' ≤ ε (step 2), and the mean value inequality on the convex B_R gives |g_{σ(i)}(w) − g_{σ(i)}(0)| ≤ ε'R ≤ ε/2, hence |g_{σ(i)}(w) − b| < ε.

6. (Domains.) Choose r_U > 0 with ball(x, 2r_U) ⊆ U (U open, x ∈ U). For R > 0 and all large i, |x_i − x| < r_U and λ_iR < r_U, so ball(x_i, λ_iR) ⊆ U and ball(0, R) = η_i(ball(x_i, λ_iR)) ⊆ η_i(U). For such i and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R), ω is a test form in η_i(U) and currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω).

7. (Mass bound: (H4).) Fix R > 0; for all large i also x_i ∈ ball(x, r₀) and λ_iR < r₀. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) be admissible with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R). By testform_corr (a) and (c) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with ω'(z) = ω(η_i(z)) for all z and S_i(ω) = λ_i^{−n}·T(ω'). Now tsupport ω' ⊆ η_i^{−1}(tsupport ω) ⊆ η_i^{−1}(ball(0, R)) = ball(x_i, λ_iR) and |ω'(z)| = |ω(η_i(z))| ≤ 1, so ω' is admissible for M_{ball(x_i,λ_iR)}(T), and (a) with y := x_i, ρ := λ_iR gives ofReal(T(ω')) ≤ T.massOn(ball(x_i, λ_iR)) ≤ ofReal(C(λ_iR)^n). Hence T(ω') ≤ c_*λ_i^nR^n and currentEval(S_i)(ω) = λ_i^{−n}T(ω') ≤ c_*R^n. So (H4) holds, also along σ, with c := c_*R^n.

8. (Representation: (H3).) Let F'_i := {w ∈ D_i : G_i(w) ∈ η_i(E)}. It is measurable: η_i(E) is measurable (η_i is a homeomorphism, E is measurable) and G_i is continuous on the open set D_i. Fix R > 0 and let i be so large that ball(0, R) ⊆ η_i(U) (step 6), |s_i| + λ_iR < δ₁ (so B_R ⊆ D_i) and ball(x_i, λ_iR) ⊆ Z (x_i → x ∈ Z, Z open, λ_i → 0). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R). By step 6 and blowup_region (y := x_i, λ := λ_i):
 currentEval(S_i)(ω) = ∫_{η_i(E)} f_i dH^{n+1}, where f_i(y) := ξ_N(x_i + λ_iy)(dω(y)).
(8a) η_i(E) ∩ ball(0, R) ⊆ G_i(F'_i ∩ B_R) ⊆ η_i(E). Let y ∈ η_i(E) with |y| < R. Then e := x_i + λ_iy ∈ E ⊆ N and |e − x_i| < λ_iR, so e ∈ N ∩ Z and by (f) e = Γ(v) with v ∈ B_{δ₁}. With w := (v − s_i)/λ_i we have s_i + λ_iw = v ∈ B_{δ₁} and G_i(w) = η_i(Γ(v)) = η_i(e) = y (step 2), so w ∈ F'_i, and |w| = |ι*y| ≤ |y| < R. The second inclusion is the definition of F'_i.
(8b) f_i vanishes outside ball(0, R), since dω = 0 outside tsupport ω. Y := G_i(F'_i ∩ B_R) is measurable (G_i is continuous and injective on D_i because ι*G_i = id; MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), and f_i = 0 on η_i(E) ∖ Y by (8a). Hence ∫_{η_i(E)} f_i dH^{n+1} = ∫_Y f_i dH^{n+1} (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero; η_i(E) is measurable).
(8c) By graph_area (m := n + 1, g := g_i, D := D_i, A := F'_i ∩ B_R): ∫_Y f_i dH^{n+1} = ∫_{F'_i∩B_R} J_i(w)·f_i(G_i(w)) dw with J_i(w) := √det(DG_i(w)*DG_i(w)).
(8d) For w ∈ F'_i ∩ B_R let v := s_i + λ_iw ∈ B_{δ₁}. By step 2, DG_i(w) = DΓ(v) and x_i + λ_iG_i(w) = Γ(v), so by (h) with α := dω(G_i(w)): J_i(w)·f_i(G_i(w)) = √det(DΓ(v)*DΓ(v))·ξ_N(Γ(v))(dω(G_i(w))) = dω(G_i(w))(DΓ(v)e) = dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e).
Hence currentEval(S_i)(ω) = ∫_{F'_i∩B_R} dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e) dw for every such ω: this is (H3), also along σ.

9. (Conclusion via flat_limit.) Apply flat_limit with U'_i := η_{σ(i)}(U), S'_i := S_{σ(i)}, g'_i := g_{σ(i)}, F''_i := F'_{σ(i)} (measurable), the offset b of step 4 and ξ_A := ξ_N(x), which satisfies ξ_A(α) = α(ιe) by (g). Its hypotheses hold: orthogonality and spanning by (d); S_{σ(i)} ⇀ S, since a subsequence of a sequence with currentEval(S_i)(ω) → S(ω) has the same limits; (H1) and (H2) by step 5; (H3) by step 8; (H4) by step 7. flat_limit yields a measurable F ⊆ {y : ∃ w, y = ιw + ι'b} with IsBoundaryOfRegion S F (y ↦ ξ_N(x)); together with b this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: In chart coordinates the blow-ups see the rescaled graphs G_i(w) = ιw + ι'λ_i^{−1}(u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i), with DG_i(w) = DΓ(s_i + λ_iw) and x_i + λ_iG_i(w) = Γ(s_i + λ_iw).
Bounded offsets |p_i − x_i| ≤ C₀λ_i and the mean value inequality bound g_i(0); a subsequence has g_{σ(i)}(0) → b, and Du(0) = 0 gives C¹ convergence g_{σ(i)} → b on every ball.
testform_corr and the mass hypothesis give currentEval(S_i)(ω) ≤ c_*R^n for admissible ω supported in ball(0, R).
blowup_region, N ∩ Z = Γ(B_{δ₁}), graph_area and the orientation formula give currentEval(S_i)(ω) = ∫_{F'_i∩B_R} dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e) dw.
flat_limit turns these properties into S = ∂[[F]] with F in the plane {ιw + ι'b} and constant orientation ξ_N(x).
